title: GATE 2027 Mechanical (ME): Dates, Syllabus, Cut-offs, Plan
summary: GATE 2027 ME: official dates (6-21 Feb), fees, revised syllabus, marking, 2026 topic weightage, cut-offs, a 12-week plan and PSU recruitment.
body_markdown:
GATE 2027 is organised by IIT Madras and will be held on 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21 February 2027, with results on 19 March 2027. Registration has closed: the regular window ran from 2 September to 5 October 2026 and the late-fee window to 12 October. The Mechanical Engineering (ME) paper is a 3-hour, 65-question, 100-mark computer-based test, and its syllabus has been revised for 2027. The date of the ME paper itself has not been announced yet, so plan for the first exam day: that leaves about 12 weeks from today.


> **GATE 2027 ME at a glance (as of 14 Nov 2026)**
>
>
> - **Organising institute:** IIT Madras, on behalf of the National Coordination Board (GATE), Ministry of Education. GATE 2027 is the 45th edition.
> - **Exam days:** 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21 February 2027, forenoon (9:30 am to 12:30 pm) and afternoon (2:30 pm to 5:30 pm) sessions. Paper-wise schedule: not yet published.
> - **Still open:** free defect rectification until 30 November 2026; the paid data-correction window closes today, 14 November.
> - **Exam city slip:** 4 January 2027. **Admit card:** date not yet announced. **Results:** 19 March 2027.
> - **Paper:** 65 questions, 100 marks: General Aptitude 15, Engineering Mathematics 13, core mechanical 72. Negative marking only on MCQs.
> - **Last year's ME cut-off:** 25.2 marks (General) in GATE 2026; 10,970 of 59,612 candidates qualified.


This guide covers the official dates and fees, the full ME syllabus with what changed for 2027, how the paper is marked, where the marks actually fell in the 2026 ME paper, a realistic 12-week plan, and how public sector undertakings (PSUs) use GATE scores to hire mechanical engineers.


## When is GATE 2027, and who is conducting it?


IIT Madras is the organising institute for GATE 2027; the exam is conducted jointly by IISc and the IITs for the National Coordination Board, Ministry of Education. The official website is[gate2027.iitm.ac.in](https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in/) and applications are handled on the GOAPS portal.


GATE 2027 key dates from the official important-dates page (14 Nov 2026). IIT Madras notes that all dates are liable to change.


The registration dates moved twice. The portal was first announced for 14 August, then 27 August, and finally opened on 2 September 2026. The table below lists the current dates; the official page shows the earlier ones struck through.

**When is the ME paper?** Not announced yet. The brochure says the complete schedule will be notified later. For reference, in GATE 2026 (organised by IIT Guwahati) Mechanical Engineering was a single-session paper on Saturday 14 February 2026, afternoon session. Do not assume the same slot this year; check the official site when the paper-wise schedule is released.

## What is the GATE 2027 ME exam pattern and marking scheme?


Item Detail


Mode and language Computer-based test, English only, on-screen virtual scientific calculator (no physical calculator)


Duration 3 hours (PwD candidates eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour)


Questions 65: 10 General Aptitude + 55 subject


Marks 100: General Aptitude 15 (5 × 1 + 5 × 2), Engineering Mathematics 13, core ME 72


Question types MCQ (one correct of four), MSQ (one or more correct), NAT (type a number)


Negative marking MCQ only: −1/3 for a wrong 1-mark answer, −2/3 for a wrong 2-mark answer. None for MSQ or NAT. No partial marks.


Score validity 3 years from the result date


The mix of question types matters for strategy. In the GATE 2026 ME paper, the answer key shows 45 MCQs (all 10 aptitude questions plus 35 subject questions) and 20 NAT questions, and **no MSQs** at all. That put 62 marks at risk of negative marking and 38 marks (all NAT) free of it. The 2027 mix may differ, but NAT questions are where guessing costs nothing and where careful arithmetic on the virtual calculator earns marks.


### How is the GATE score calculated?


The scorecard shows marks out of 100 and a GATE score out of 1,000. The score rescales your marks between the qualifying mark and the average of the top candidates:


**GATE score = 350 + (900 − 350) × (M − Mq) / (Mt − Mq)**


Here M is your mark (normalised if the paper runs in several sessions), Mq the General-category qualifying mark, and Mt the mean of the top 0.1% or top 10 candidates, whichever group is larger. For 2027, the General qualifying mark is max(25, min(40, μ + σ)), where μ and σ are the mean and standard deviation of all candidates in the paper; OBC-NCL/EWS candidates qualify at 90% of that and SC/ST/PwD at two-thirds.


**Worked example with GATE 2026 ME numbers** (Mq = 25.2, Mt = 74.58, from the official performance report):


Marks GATE score


25.2 (cut-off) 350


30 ≈ 404


40 ≈ 515


50 ≈ 626


60 ≈ 738


74.58 (top-0.1% average) 900


So in 2026, every extra 10 marks above the cut-off was worth about 111 score points. The constants change every year with the paper's difficulty, which is why PSUs and IITs compare scores (or marks within the same year), never marks across years.


## What is the GATE 2027 ME syllabus?


The official ME syllabus has four sections, plus the General Aptitude section common to all papers. Below is the full content, condensed only in wording; the PDF on the official site is the authority.


### Section 1: Engineering Mathematics (13 marks)


- **Linear algebra:** matrix algebra, systems of linear equations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- **Calculus:** functions of a single variable, limit, continuity, differentiability, mean value theorems, indeterminate forms; definite and improper integrals; double and triple integrals; partial and total derivatives, Taylor series in one and two variables, maxima and minima, Fourier series; gradient, divergence, curl, vector identities, directional derivatives, line, surface and volume integrals, Gauss, Stokes and Green theorems.
- **Differential equations:** first-order (linear and nonlinear), higher-order linear with constant coefficients, Euler-Cauchy, initial and boundary value problems, Laplace transforms, solutions of the heat, wave and Laplace equations.
- **Complex variables:** analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, Cauchy's integral theorem and contour integral formula, Taylor and Laurent series.
- **Probability and statistics:** probability definitions, sampling theorems, conditional probability, mean, median, mode, standard deviation, random variables, binomial, Poisson and normal distributions.
- **Numerical methods:** linear and nonlinear algebraic equations, trapezoidal and Simpson's rules, single- and multi-step methods for ODEs.


### Section 2: Applied Mechanics and Design


- **Engineering mechanics:** free-body diagrams and equilibrium; friction including rolling resistance, belt-pulley, brakes, clutches, screw jack, wedge, vehicles; plane trusses and frames; virtual work; plane kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies; impulse, momentum and energy methods.
- **Mechanics of materials:** stress, strain and elastic constants; 2D stress and strain transformation; Mohr's circle; thin-walled pressure vessels; shear force and bending moment diagrams; bending and shear stresses; shear centre; beam deflection; torsion of circular shafts; Euler columns; energy methods; thermal stresses; strain gauges and rosettes; mechanical properties, toughness, hardness, impact strength.
- **Theory of machines:** displacement, velocity and acceleration analysis of plane mechanisms; dynamic analysis of linkages; cams; gears and gear trains; flywheels and governors; balancing; gyroscope.
- **Vibrations:** free and forced vibration of linear single- and two-degree-of-freedom systems; damping estimation; isolation and transmissibility; resonance; critical speeds of shafts; **control systems, PID controller, transfer function** .
- **Machine design:** static and dynamic loading; failure theories; fatigue and the S-N diagram; bolted, riveted and welded joints; shafts, gears, belt drives, rolling and sliding bearings, brakes and clutches, springs.


### Section 3: Fluid Mechanics and Thermal Sciences


- **Fluid mechanics:** fluid properties; statics, forces on submerged bodies, stability of floating bodies; control-volume mass, momentum and energy; fluid acceleration; differential continuity and momentum equations; velocity potential; Bernoulli; dimensional analysis; viscous incompressible flow, boundary layer, elementary turbulence, pipe flow and losses; one-dimensional high-speed compressible flow; converging and converging-diverging nozzles.
- **Heat transfer:** modes; 1D conduction, thermal resistance, fins; unsteady conduction and lumped systems; thermal boundary layer; dimensionless groups and correlations for free and forced convection over plates and in pipes; boiling and condensation; heat exchangers (LMTD and NTU); radiation, Stefan-Boltzmann and Wien laws, black and grey surfaces, view factors, radiation networks.
- **Thermodynamics:** systems and processes; pure substances; ideal and real gases; zeroth, first and second laws; work, heat, energy and entropy changes; closed and open system analysis; property tables and charts; availability and irreversibility; thermodynamic relations.
- **Applications:** vapour and gas power cycles with regeneration and reheat; air-standard Otto, Diesel and dual cycles; basics of combustion (air-fuel ratio, equivalence ratio); vapour and gas refrigeration and heat pumps; psychrometry; turbomachinery (impulse and reaction, velocity diagrams, Pelton, Francis and Kaplan turbines, steam and gas turbines, compressors, pumps and pump characteristics).


### Section 4: Materials, Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering


- **Engineering materials:** crystal structure of common metals, phase diagrams, heat treatment; properties and uses of metals, alloys, polymers, composites and ceramics; engineering and true stress-strain diagrams.
- **Casting, forming and joining:** casting processes, patterns, moulds and cores, solidification, riser and gating design, casting defects; plastic deformation and yield criteria; hot and cold working; bulk and sheet forming and load estimation; powder metallurgy; welding, brazing, soldering, solid-state welding, adhesive bonding; non-destructive testing.
- **Machining:** machining operations and machine tools; single- and multi-point tools; tool geometry in ASA and ORS systems; mechanics of machining; tool materials, tool life and wear; economics of machining; abrasive and non-traditional processes; work holding, jigs and fixtures.
- **Additive manufacturing:** principles of AM processes; advantages, limitations and applications of AM products.
- **Metrology and inspection:** limits, fits and tolerances; linear and angular measurement; comparators; interferometry; form and finish; alignment testing; tolerance analysis; principle of the CMM.
- **Computer-aided manufacturing and automation:** CAD/CAM integration; NC/CNC machines and programming; pneumatic, electro-pneumatic and hydraulic actuators; programmable logic controllers (PLCs).
- **Production planning and control:** work study, productivity, forecasting, aggregate planning, scheduling, MRP, six sigma, lean; inventory control (deterministic models, safety stock); quality and reliability.
- **Operations research:** linear programming and simplex, transportation, assignment, network flow, simple queuing, PERT and CPM.


### What changed in the GATE 2027 ME syllabus?


IIT Madras says the syllabi have been revised for the first time in five years. We compared the 2027 ME PDF with the GATE 2026 ME PDF line by line. The structure and most topics are the same; the changes worth adjusting your plan for are:


Area New or expanded in 2027 Dropped from the wording


Vibrations Two-degree-of-freedom systems, damping estimation, transmissibility; control systems, PID controller, transfer function (was single-degree-of-freedom only)


Engineering mechanics Rolling resistance (in place of rolling friction), plane trusses Lagrange's equation


Mechanics of materials 2D stress and strain transformation; mechanical properties, toughness, hardness, impact strength Testing on the universal testing machine (as a separate item)


Machine design Belt drives None


Fluid mechanics Velocity potential; 1D high-speed compressible flow; converging and converging-diverging nozzles (was "basics of compressible flow") None


Heat transfer Boiling and condensation Heisler charts


Applications Basics of combustion (air-fuel ratio, equivalence ratio); pump characteristics None


Materials and manufacturing Crystal structure; polymers, composites, ceramics; true stress-strain; casting defects; solid-state welding; NDT; tool geometry (ASA, ORS); additive manufacturing as its own topic None


Automation and IE Pneumatic, electro-pneumatic and hydraulic actuators; PLCs; work study, productivity, six sigma, quality and reliability "Computer integrated manufacturing" renamed


The practical reading: control systems/PID, two-DOF vibration, nozzles, boiling and condensation, combustion basics, PLCs and actuators, and NDT are the topics with no previous-year GATE ME questions to practise from. Budget a few hours for each from standard textbooks rather than skipping them.


## Which ME topics carry the most marks?


GATE does not publish topic-wise weightage. To get a real number, we took the official GATE 2026 ME master question paper and answer key, assigned each of the 55 subject questions to one topic of the 2027 syllabus, and summed the marks. The classification is ours (a few questions straddle two topics; we chose the closer one), but the marks per question come straight from the key.


Marks per topic in the GATE 2026 ME paper (Skill-Lync classification of the official paper; marks from the official key). General Aptitude adds 15.


Three things stand out:


- **The three core sections were exactly balanced:** 24 marks each for Applied Mechanics and Design, Fluid and Thermal Sciences, and Materials, Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering. No section is skippable.
- **Aptitude plus maths is 28 marks.** Both are fixed by the brochure (15 and 13), and they are the most predictable marks in the paper.
- **Industrial engineering was worth 10 marks** (production planning, inventory and operations research). These are short, formula-driven questions: forecasting, EOQ, PERT, LP duality. They reward a week of focused practice more than almost any other topic.


One paper is one sample. Topic marks move by a few each year, so use this to rank topics, not to drop any.


## What score do you need in GATE ME?


To *qualify* , very little: the 2026 General cut-off was 25.2 marks. To be *competitive* for top IIT M.Tech seats or PSU shortlists, far more, because the field is wide and most candidates score low.


How GATE 2026 ME candidates scored. 2,521 candidates (4.2%) scored 40 or more and 888 (1.5%) scored 50 or more. GATE year (organiser) Registered Appeared Cut-off General OBC-NCL/EWS SC/ST/PwD


2024 (IISc) 83,114 65,546 28.6 25.7 19.0


2025 (IIT Roorkee) 79,830 62,015 35.8 32.2 23.8


2026 (IIT Guwahati) 76,823 59,612 25.2 22.6 16.7


Two trends: ME registrations have fallen each year (83,114 to 76,823 over two cycles), and the cut-off swings by 10 marks with paper difficulty. In 2026 the mean ME mark was 13.35 with a standard deviation of 11.86, so the cut-off (μ + σ) landed at 25.2; the highest mark was 96.67. For perspective, in 2026 a mark of 40 or more put a candidate in the top 4.2% of ME candidates, and 50 or more in the top 1.5%. NTPC's General-category shortlist for mechanical trainees sat in that range, as the PSU section below shows; the exact bar depends on the organisation, the year and your category.


## How to prepare for GATE 2027 ME in the 12 weeks left


From 14 November 2026 to 6 February 2027 is exactly 84 days. If you have studied the core subjects in college, 12 weeks is enough to turn that into exam marks; it is not enough to learn everything from zero, so the plan below prioritises by marks and by how quickly a topic converts into correct answers.


A 12-week plan weighted by the 2026 marks. Daily: 30 minutes of General Aptitude and 20 revision questions from earlier weeks.


### The plan, week by week


1. **This weekend (14-15 Nov):** fix your application if the portal flags a defect (free until 30 November), download the 2026 ME paper and key from the official site, and set up an error log (a spreadsheet with question, topic, why you got it wrong).
2. **Week 1 (16-22 Nov):** sit the GATE 2026 ME paper in 3 hours, using only an on-screen calculator. Mark it. Your topic-wise losses decide the order of weeks 2 to 9. Start maths: linear algebra and calculus.
3. **Weeks 2-4 (23 Nov-13 Dec):** Applied Mechanics and Design, 24 marks. Engineering mechanics and strength of materials first (15 of the 24 in 2026), then machine design, theory of machines and vibrations. Add the new items: two-DOF systems, transmissibility, and enough control theory to handle a transfer function and a PID question.
4. **Weeks 5-7 (14 Dec-3 Jan):** Fluid and Thermal, 24 marks. Thermodynamics with cycles and the new combustion basics; fluid mechanics with compressible flow and nozzles; heat transfer last (it was the biggest single thermal topic in 2026). First full mock at the end of week 7.
5. **Weeks 8-9 (4-17 Jan):** Materials, Manufacturing and IE, 24 marks. Machining and forming numericals, then metrology, additive manufacturing, CNC and PLC basics, and a hard push on production planning, inventory and operations research.
6. **Week 10 (18-24 Jan):** remaining maths (differential equations, complex variables, probability, numerical methods) and a sweep of previous-year ME questions by topic. Two full mocks.
7. **Week 11 (25-31 Jan):** three timed full mocks in the same time slot as your exam session. After each, redo every wrong and every guessed question from the error log.
8. **Week 12 (1-6 Feb):** formula sheets, one light mock, normal sleep. If your ME paper turns out to be on 13-14 or 20-21 February, extend weeks 10 and 11, not the new-topic weeks.


### Rules that matter more than the timetable


- **Do aptitude every day.** 15 marks, five 1-mark and five 2-mark questions, no syllabus to finish. Thirty minutes a day for 12 weeks is enough to make it near-certain marks.
- **Attack NAT questions with care, MCQs with judgement.** No negative marking on NAT, so never leave one blank if you have a reasonable approach. On a 2-mark MCQ a wrong answer costs 0.67; guess only when you can eliminate two options.
- **Practise on the virtual calculator.** The exam allows only the on-screen calculator, and IIT Madras says the virtual calculator and mock tests will be available through the official site. Doing 12 weeks of practice on a phone calculator and then switching on exam day costs time.
- **Use previous-year papers as the main question bank.** The official site hosts past ME papers and keys. The syllabus barely changed in most topics, so they remain the best practice set.


If a subject from college is weak, it is usually thermodynamics or design. Our[Foundations of Thermodynamics](https://skill-lync.com/mechanical-engineering-courses/foundations-thermodynamics-industrial-applications) course covers cycles, refrigeration and property relations in an applied way, and the[structural analysis](https://skill-lync.com/mechanical-engineering-courses/structural-analysis-using-ansys-workbench-mechanical) course connects mechanics of materials to how stresses are checked in industry. They are not GATE coaching, but they make the theory stick.

### Which well-known PSUs do not currently hire ME through GATE?


- **IOCL** : its 2026 engineer recruitment (advert of 14 Aug 2026) is through its own computer-based test, weighted 85% CBT, 5% group discussion and task, 10% interview.
- **ONGC** : recruits engineers through its own CBT since 2025; its last GATE-based round used GATE 2023 scores.
- **SAIL** and **HPCL** : own CBT followed by GD and interview.
- **BHEL** : the latest GATE-based engineer trainee recruitment on its careers portal is from GATE 2018.
- **POWERGRID** , **AAI** and **Coal India** use GATE, but their recent GATE adverts did not include Mechanical.


Coaching material and older blog posts still list these as GATE routes for mechanical engineers. Read the PSU's current advert before you plan around one.

## GATE ME or a core industry job: which path after 2027?


A good GATE score opens three doors: M.Tech or MS at IITs, IISc and NITs (with a Ministry of Education stipend at eligible institutes), PSU jobs that shortlist on GATE scores, and some direct recruitment in central government that now uses GATE. None of them is guaranteed by qualifying alone; the brochure itself says GATE qualification does not assure a PSU job.


Many mechanical graduates also go straight into private-sector design, simulation and manufacturing roles, and some do both: write GATE in February and keep building skills that employers test. If that is your plan, the most useful skills alongside GATE preparation are CAD, GD&T and simulation. See our[GD&T interview questions](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/top-10-gdt-interview-questions) guide and[how to get a core mechanical job after graduation](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/how-to-get-a-core-mechanical-engineering-job-after-graduation) , or programmes such as the[PG Program in CAD](https://skill-lync.com/mechanical-engineering-courses/masters-design) and[PG Program in CAE](https://skill-lync.com/mechanical-engineering-courses/masters-cae) .


## Frequently asked questions


### When is the GATE 2027 Mechanical Engineering exam?


GATE 2027 runs on 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21 February 2027. The date and session for the ME paper had not been announced as of 14 November 2026; IIT Madras will publish the paper-wise schedule on gate2027.iitm.ac.in.


### Can I still apply for GATE 2027?


No. Regular registration closed on 5 October, the late-fee period on 12 October and a special window on 16 October 2026. If you applied, the free defect-rectification window is open until 30 November 2026.


### Has the GATE 2027 ME syllabus changed?


Yes, modestly. New or expanded topics include two-DOF vibrations and control systems (PID, transfer functions), compressible flow through nozzles, boiling and condensation, combustion basics, PLCs and actuators, NDT and additive manufacturing. Lagrange's equation and Heisler charts no longer appear in the wording.


### Is there negative marking in GATE ME?


Only on MCQs: one-third of the marks for a wrong 1-mark answer, two-thirds for a wrong 2-mark answer. MSQ and NAT questions have no negative marking. In the 2026 ME paper, 38 of the 100 marks were NAT questions.


### What was the GATE 2026 ME cut-off?


25.2 marks for General, 22.6 for OBC-NCL/EWS and 16.7 for SC/ST/PwD, with 10,970 of 59,612 candidates qualifying. In 2025 it was 35.8, and in 2024, 28.6.


### How long is a GATE score valid?


Three years from the result date. GATE 2027 results are due on 19 March 2027, so the score will be usable until March 2030. Each PSU, however, states which GATE year it accepts in its own advertisement.
